 Order

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR pertaining to Crime No. 132/2023 registered by PS MIG Colony, Distt. Indore(Urban) for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC with all consequential proceedings thereto,
on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.

2. The exposition of the facts giving rise to the present petition is as under :
As per case of prosecution, Rahul S/o Prem Arora, resident of Flat no. 102, Gaurav Apartment, Anoop Nagar, Indore submitted a written NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:12323 complaint at the P.S. MIG Colony Indore on 31.01.2022 alleging forgery of a will by his Uncle - Sushil Arora.
It is stated in the complaint that his Grand Father Shri Purushottam Lal Arora had expired on 01.07.2007 at his residence in MIG Colony, Indore.

After death of Purushottam Lal Arora, his uncle Sunil Arora informed the family that Late Shri Purushottam Lal Arora had executed a will dated 24.01.2007 and bequeathed his property to Sushil Arora and his wife Alka Sushil Arora vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116484087/
1 Arora.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: His father, Prem Arora, filed a Civil Suit No. 74/2008 before the District Judge, Indore challenging the will.
Sushil Arora proposed compromise in the matter and issued three post dated cheques for an amount of Rs. 45 Lakhs for settlement.

His father had withdrawn the civil suit because of the compromise, but his uncle Susheel Kumar Arora resiled from the compromise and submitted a written complaint at the P.S. MIG Colony, Indore relating to theft of cheques.

When execution of will was inquired, it was revealed that the stamp was issued on 03.10.2007 and the will was executed on 13.04.2007 i.e. four months after the death of his Grand Father Late Shri Purushottam Lal Arora.
The will is suspicious.

The P.S.
MIG Colony, Indore(Urban) registered FIR at Crime No. 132/2023 for offence punishable u/S 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC against Sushil Arora and Alka Arora.
Relevant documents were seized.
The statements of witnesses were recorded.

Although, the attesting witness verifies execution of will by Shri Purushottam Lal Arora and no record with regard to issuance of the stamp in question was found,
other circumstantial material was collected.
Investigation is underway.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12323 3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that parties have amicably settled their disputes relating to ancestral property.
The complainant has filed a civil suit vide RCS No. B/547/2018 in which the compromise has been executed between the parties.
The dispute is purely civil in nature and does not constitute a criminal offence.
They wish to proceed with life and accord a quietus to the dispute among the family members.
4. The parties have submitted application - I.A. No.2429/2025 under Section 320 of Cr.P.C. seeking permission for compromise alongwith affidavits sworn by both the parties.
5. In compliance of the order 21.03.2025 of this Court, the factum of compromise has been verified by the Principal Registrar of this Court.
The statements of petitioners - Susheel Arora and Alka Arora as well as of Complainants - Rahul Arora S/o Prem Arora and Prem Arora S/o Late Shri Purushottam Lal Arora were recorded.
The Principal Registrar has submitted report dated 25.03.2025 that the parties have arrived at compromise voluntarily without any threat, inducement or coercion.

6. In the cases of Jagdish Channa & Others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & Others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise,
criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the Court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.

sentences.text: The parties, close relatives, wish to accord a quietus to dispute.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the petitioners.
Under such a situation, 482 of Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the Courts.
More-so, the offence in question is not against the society, but merely affect the parties.
It has no bearing on public order.

8. Consequently, this Court allows this MCRC with the direction that FIR pertaining to Crime No.
132/2023 registered by P.S. MIG Colony, Distt. Indore for offences punishable under Sections 420,
467, 468 and 471 of IPC and all other subsequent proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed with regard to petitioners - Susheel Arora and Alka Arora.
9. This petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. stands disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
